title: He is no jazz historian
summary: He declines to name high points of jazz, having not paid attention for much of his life.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: I'm looking for a profound observation on today's music, but there is no today music--start typing now, lady. There is no today's music.
Starting in 1900--let's do the birth of the blues, starting in 1900, what are significant high points, according to George Handy?
Am I beating you to death, or would you like to do this?
You're kicking the shit out of me.
Would you like to do it or shall we turn this thing off?

I don't think I'm capable of handling that, simply because I don't know. I'm not a good jazz historian at all, and for a great period of my life I didn't pay attention, I wasn't involved constantly. I was just involved at small moments in time, although I
managed to keep working through that time; still I wasn't looking around, I didn't notice who else was on the scene, didn't listen to what else was being done and I wasn't interested.
I'm learning in these last few years what went on. I'm discovering things that people are astounded I didn't know.
Some of the new people that I wasn't aware of, some of the things that had been recorded that I wasn't aware of.
